hints: Focus on the type of alcohol formed in each case, remember primary means the OH carbon is attached to only one other carbon.
Notice that propanone is a ketone and propene hydrates by Markovnikov addition, so both point toward a secondary alcohol.
Recall what strong reduction of a carboxylic acid gives, and what vigorous oxidation with hot concentrated KMnO4 does to an alkene.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes an alcohol primary**

A primary alcohol has the -OH group on a carbon joined to only one other carbon. Think $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-OH}$. Let's test each reaction for this pattern.

Rule to use:
$$\text{primary} = \text{-CH}_2\text{OH}, \quad \text{secondary} = \text{-CH(OH)-}$$

**Check reduction and hydration routes**

Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone. $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces it to propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. Propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$, with steam and $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ adds $\text{H-OH}$ by Markovnikov rule to give propan-2-ol again, also secondary.

Equations:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$

**Check strong reduction vs strong oxidation**

Butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is reduced all the way to butan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which is primary. Ethene with hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is oxidatively cleaved to $\text{CO}_2$ and water, so no alcohol forms.

Equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

options.A: Propanone is a ketone. NaBH4 reduces the C=O to CH-OH in the middle of the chain to give propan-2-ol, which is a secondary alcohol, not primary.
options.B: Hydration of propene follows Markovnikov addition where OH adds to the more substituted carbon. This gives propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol, not primary.
options.C: LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent that reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols. Butanoic acid gives butan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2CH2OH, where the OH carbon is attached to only one other carbon.
options.D: Hot concentrated acidified KMnO4 is very vigorous oxidation. It cleaves the C=C bond of ethene completely to give CO2 and H2O, so no alcohol product is obtained.
